Indolent

IN-duh-lent · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Indolent is wanting to avoid activity or exertion.

The cat spent the entire afternoon in an indolent sprawl across the windowsill, ignoring every toy we dangled in front of it.

Worked Example

Despite his coach's warnings, the indolent player skipped every optional practice all season and was benched by playoffs.

Indolent describes a habitual preference for avoiding effort, not a single tired afternoon.

How Indolent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

lazy

Antonyms

industrious

How Strong Is It? — relaxed → indolent → indolent

relaxed vs. indolent

relaxed vs. indolent: Taking one lazy Sunday off is relaxed.

indolent vs. indolent

indolent vs. indolent: An indolent employee who avoids every task, every day, is a real problem.

Now place each word on the right side of indolent.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin)

root+suffix — dolent

root+suffix — dolent: feeling pain or grief (Latin (dolere))

Put it together

Put it together: in- ("not") + dolent ("feeling pain") = literally "feeling no pain" -- originally, avoiding effort so as not to suffer, which gave us today's sense of "lazy."

Use the root in a new word: dolorous

Use the root in a new word: dolorous: The same root survives in the rarer word "dolorous," meaning full of sorrow or grief.
